1. Case 1: Prion disease most likely
The patient's 3-year progressive CNS disorder with autonomic dysfunction is most consistent with a CNS neurodegenerative process. The leading specific refinement is prion disease, supported by convergence of radiologic, laboratory, and clinical evidence. MSA and hereditary spinocerebellar ataxia are less likely; immune-mediated ataxia, peripheral autonomic neuropathy, and toxic/metabolic encephalopathy are largely refuted by non-inflammatory CSF, central autonomic failure, and absence of toxic exposure. However, the 3-year course is atypical, and confirmatory tests including RT-QuIC, 14-3-3, EEG, and PRNP are pending, so prion disease remains probable rather than definitively confirmed.
